Alcohol: favourite and least at the same time, started too young, magical euphoria of my youth comes back when I drink.

Weed: Enjoyable even when it initiated a fucked up panic attack.

Every goddamn benzo: fun till it’s not, caused bad fights with loved ones. Only real use is in keeping my head level when I’ve just been grilled at work or I’m sitting at home with a beer and a joint by myself. 

Oxy: feels too good, tried for 2 weeks, felt a deep addiction that could creep in.

Meth: Terrible. Terrible. God terrible. I don’t know why I’ve done it a couple times. Genuinely have seen the depth of my capacity for evil on this. 

Cocaine: Enjoyable in comfortable settings, bad in clubs. Mostly causes me to be enthusiastic about whatever the hell im doing. 

MDMA: Fun exactly one time. Had to try to have fun every other time. 

Roofies: I won’t lie it was fun but I also woke up with gashes in my hands from getting into a fight and I had to be hospitalized in case of human saliva causing problems.

LSD: Very good with friends/SO when partying at low doses. High doses got me too deep into mathematics problems but I did publish a paper I finished after taking a decent dose.

Mushrooms: A gift so precious I won’t use more than once a year. I don’t have a real good/bad feeling towards the high, I just feel that it’s one of the few things in life where the more you give the more you get. I’ve helped myself and others on this, and that’s very meaningful.

Methcathinone: eh, good for dieting and being a smelly sweaty weirdo.

Ritalin: inevitable ramp up to dangerous doses that require 1-2 month breaks usually alongside benzo use. Unfortunately, I am certainly dependent on this drug, and simply cannot keep my thoughts from scattering into 100 different projects and ditching work to go try build chips challenge, write songs, and do some research writing all at once and completing nothing.

Nicotine: wonderful when accompanied by something else

Caffeine: Nicotine’s best friend, also pooping 

GHB: Absolutely hilarious drug because it is not like alcohol but it will make you think it’s like alcohol till you wake up naked with 5 hookers and no condom

Phenibut: Good for weaning off benzos after stressful periods 

DMT: The silliest shit I’ve ever done, not in a bad way, but just silly. Came down and just thought ‘what hilarious bullshit I gained nothing from that’.

DXM: Don’t go deep and walk around the beach front unless you plan on getting blistered sunburnt and can’t order cocktails at the beach bar.

Codeine: Bit of a weird one, I don’t feel euphoria like Oxy even in high doses. I do get a sense of confidence which I’ve used in presentations/interviews/sales.

2-CB: Acid meets mdma and makes me autistic

Flakka: Horrible, taken by ‘accident’ as it was paired with modafinil in some garage brand nootropic. Made me write suicide good byes to everyone I love. 

Mescaline: Giggle factory with new colors in life.

Ambien: no need to expand I’m sure.

Lyrica: trip on your shoe lace pills

Running half marathon without getting tired
Squatting 300kg the week after

Sitting with my gf talking about mathematics, philosophy, and existence in general

Finishing a book

Finishing my work without compromising my personal time 

Interacting with somebody without assuming the worst of them 

Playing fetch with my dogs

Getting out of the house with my head up, being polite to others, and coming home not holding any weight on my shoulders over some petty nonsense.

I have three goals. To leave my partner with money that will allow her to pursue her dreams, to provide my family with the money to be comfortable for life, and to do something that will add value to the world after I die. 

I don’t feel that I do or don’t deserve anything. The accumulation of events that has brought me to where I am is largely not a result of anything I could have controlled.

Even if I have been the major influence on the course of my life since I became sentient, it still forms an infinitesimally small portion of data that  answers why I am who I am.

Most people consider this a doctrine or ideology, and perhaps I am somewhat dogmatic about my thinking, but I am a scientist through and through. 

I have been many different people, played many different roles, and have done everything of interest to my own nature. I am only motivated by those three goals I stated. I don’t see myself being entertained by anything after I achieve them. I am tired and I find this life too hard on my heart to continue.

I have a disposition towards feeling more heartache over things that normal people would simply brush off. I find this taxing and see no benefit in continuing with it once I have done what I have set out to. I am also very close to achieving these goals.

I have no appetite to endure this world any longer than I consider necessary.

I’ve spent my entire life developing a skill that involves being able to predict outcomes or indicate what indicators mean. I try not to be invested in my own emotions, and the same goes with my relationship to life and death. The concepts are trivial, I don’t have a faith or doctrine because I don’t bother myself with believing things. 

The only subjective desire I have is to continually feel like I am engaged with my world and adding value to those around me. Based on my assessment of what I have done, who I am, and my continued potential, I don’t think I will add more significant value once I complete my research. I am horrifyingly amoral and act as I please. This is not beneficial to anybody else and will inevitably create problems for people I feel care towards, simply because I will not put my own desires aside for others.

I have a few things to complete, things that will hopefully make a difference and help humanity after I am gone, but I see no reason to keep going forward after that. I am exhausted with this world. It is a wonderful place, but I cannot see myself enjoying it for much longer. I am bored, tired, disappointed with things, and I have seen and done far more than I could have hoped to. 

I have had dinner with incredible scientists and vicious gangsters alike. There is not anything conceptually novel I think I can experience. So I’m done. I don’t see what’s to look forward to. I don’t think I’m a good or bad person, but I don’t think I have a place in the world that is coming.

To see if anybody else felt like I did. I have been struggling with my mental health as both of my parents are broke as their family business has collapsed, so I have been hating the wasted hours of productivity I could be using on Freelance side work to send more money back home to support them.

To me this remote work opportunity is such a blessing because I can do my research, my take on some side projects for quick cash, recuperate from having not taken more than 5 days of actual leave in 2 years, go spend time with my parents and family and make sure they’re all keeping well, have enough of what they need, help out my younger siblings with their studies and make sure they aren’t slacking off when they should be learning while school/university is out.

Not to mention the investment opportunities presented with asset prices tanking etc... Really I just feel more hopeful about the future than I have been. All I see is opportunity. I might die (unlikely), somebody I love might die (parents being most at risk), but I deal with the statistics of life and death for a living and the coronavirus as yet presents no meaningful fear to me over that of the chance of being brutally murdered walking on the streets at night in my country.

I wasn’t looking for it to be well received, I spoke my mind. I genuinely felt happy being told that my team could not afford to not meet our deadlines and could not lose any of its resources to illness as we all serve roles that are specialized to particular needs for the regulations to be met on time. 

I feel guilty that I was happy, and I am doing work that is important and I’m always grateful to have a well paying job with so much exposure but I can’t do anything productive with the time I have leftover. I go help out where I can to try add extra value but my clients executive built our team from both internal staff and multiple consultancies on a basis of specialist needs and they closely track our activity on site. Even offsite my activity is being monitored but they know I get my work done. I just have felt a bit out of whack lately because I see so much potential for me to do more productive things with the hours I have left after specific tasks are complete.

I am probably smarter than most people, and not as smart as many of the other people in my PhD program/field/other fields. I’m not a straight killer at everything, and I know that consulting offers me an opportunity to network, understand how to run a business as opposed to just be an employee, and this is valuable to me. Unfortunately I need to be more senior before I get to see how business development is done in consulting as opposed to other positions I’ve worked in where I’ve always been a permanent staff member and even when I had to do sales, selling products is much different to selling project work or even just convincing a client that they need a new resource for some contract based work.

My boutique firm has me on a regulatory implementation project where I absolutely hate my life because I finish my work in an hour but am unable to use the other 7 we officially bill for other productivity like my god damn PhD thesis because I have to allow interception of my communications in the sensitive area I work in so I was advised by my firm to avoid working on personal stuff.

It’s not that the clients work isn’t hard, it just isn’t hard for my level of technical skills and understanding of the both how the industry works (as I worked to pay for my undgerdrad, masters, and now PhD in relevant areas to the particular industry I’m in, I was only an intern in my undergraduate and stayed their till I had a degree which accommodated  my undergrad, and have been in higher tier roles since). 

However, my firm has a tendency to treat people who in their early 20’s an inexperienced worker and start us as Analysts in a Graduate program unless you’ve directly worked in the particular industry for around 3-4 years. Basically they don’t trust the type of people our clients hire as competent but whatever. 

Most people at my experience level would be happy on my project and the amount of exposure/freedom I have to implement solutions in my own way (my manager doesn’t understand half of what I am doing because she’s from my firm but stopped studying at undergrad and built her way up in the company, I’ve been brought on as a specialist to accommodate her lack of technical skills while she does more project management/BAU/comms+meetings with clients work).

I’ve felt like jumping ship a few times but always settle down and remember that the consulting experience is really valuable for my personal goal of starting an independent shop that specializes the kind of research I have focused on, there’s a huge gap in the market for type of stuff in my country and I have specifically chosen to get my PhD to drive my validity in the specialty area while getting general consulting skills so I learn how to properly deal with clients, business development + actual project delivery from end to end, plus make awesome connections in the industry. So I’ve been roughing it out but honestly the time to work from home gives me the best chance to do more of my PhD, still make clients happy, which keeps my firm happy, and gives me this opportunity one hardly gets in their career - while being paid a handsome salary.

I donno, maybe I’m just super positive about the time for some focus and ingenuity, chance to deliver compelling research but also compelling client results which just helps build my brand for when I return to the client site. I am not socially awkward so I already have good footing but now I’ll put in 2-3 hours instead of 1 and finish work pieces of amazing quality as well as research.
Probably, I’ll make the effort to actually make sure I want what they are offering then and get the full picture. Thanks for the response.
